Import tables from files and a data dictionary

Source: R/import.R
grist_import.Rd

grist_import() creates tables in a document from a data-dict data-dict.yaml file and the Parquet, CSV or JSON files that hold the data, then loads the rows. It is the counterpart of grist_export(), and also suits data prepared elsewhere, such as lists copied out of another low-code tool.

Usage

grist_import(
  doc,
  from,
  tables = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  display = NULL,
  format = c("auto", "parquet", "csv", "json"),
  orphans = c("error", "empty"),
  if_exists = c("error", "append"),
  options = NULL
)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

from

Path to a data-dict.yaml file, or to a directory containing one. Parquet paths in the dictionary are relative to it.

tables

Names of the dictionary's tables to import. NULL imports all of them.

types

A named character vector that overrides Grist column types. Names are "Table.column", values are Grist types such as "Numeric", "Ref:People" or "RefList:Items".

display

A named character vector choosing the column a Ref or RefList column shows, e.g. c("Orders.person" = "name").

format

The format of the data files: "auto" uses whichever is found, or "parquet", "csv" or "json" to choose.

orphans

What to do with references to a key that doesn't exist in the target table: stop with an "error" before changing anything, or leave the reference "empty".

if_exists

What to do when a table already exists in the document: stop with an "error" before changing anything, or "append" rows to it. Existing tables keep their columns and types. A document made with grist_doc_create() already has an empty Table1, which counts as an existing table if the data you import also has a Table1.

options

A grist_write_options() object.

Value

A data frame with one row per imported table: table, rows and columns, invisibly. If a request fails part way, tables and rows already created remain in the document.

Column types

Grist types come from the dictionary and the data:

data-dictGrist
stringText
number, number(id)Int if the data are integers, otherwise Numeric
booleanBool
dateDate
datetimeDateTime, in the column's time_zone (UTC if it is naive or missing)
enum, list(enum)Choice, ChoiceList, with the values as choices
list(string)ChoiceList
no typeAny

Only columns described in the dictionary are imported. label and description are kept. A column named id isn't created (Grist has its own row IDs), but is used as a key if other tables refer to it. Other types, including list(number(id)), need an entry in types.

References between tables

A column with the foreign_key constraint that is part of a relationships entry (join: orders.person = people.id) becomes a Ref column. The tables are loaded first, and then each reference is rewritten from the source key to the row ID Grist assigned, so tables can be loaded in any order and may refer to themselves. The key column stays in the table as ordinary data.

data-dict can't declare foreign keys on list columns, so use types for RefList columns, e.g. types = c("Orders.items" = "RefList:Items"). The target table must have a primary_key column, whose values the list holds.

A Ref column shows its target's row ID unless you choose a column to show with display.

Data files

A table's data is read from the Parquet file named by its source in the dictionary. Tables without a source, such as those from grist_export() with format = "csv" or "json", are read from <table>.parquet, <table>.csv or <table>.json next to the dictionary, in that order, or the one format names.

Text files have no types of their own, so values are converted to the types in the dictionary (dates as YYYY-MM-DD, date-times as ISO 8601 in UTC, list columns as JSON arrays). A number column becomes Int when all of its values are whole, so a Numeric column of whole numbers needs types = c("Table.column" = "Numeric").

Requires the yaml12 package, and the nanoparquet package for Parquet files.

See also

Other export: grist_export()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("<new doc id>")
grist_import(doc, "pets-export")

grist_import(
  doc,
  "pets-export",
  types = c("Orders.buddies" = "RefList:People"),
  display = c("Orders.person" = "name")
)
}
